data.narrative:
Govini, a Growth-stage defense and security software company, has raised $174M in total capital. The comparable universe in Defense & Security includes 2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private peers, though stage-specific clustering sufficient for reliable peer multiples proved unavailable—23 same-sector peers exist, but none met minimum thresholds for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or valuation-tier matching.

Given data constraints, the Stage-Progression method represents the primary applicable triangulation approach. This method applies a 1.2x step-up multiplier to the $174M capital raised baseline, reflecting typical valuation uplift through the Growth stage to subsequent funding rounds, yielding an implied valuation of $209M. The 1.2x multiplier is calibrated to standard venture progression mechanics rather than sector-specific tailwinds.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $177M to $240M, with a median point of $209M. The low end ($177M) represents a conservative treatment of the raised capital; the median reflects stage-standard progression; the high end incorporates upside scenarios consistent with peer-set positioning. Key uncertainties include the absence of reliable same-stage peer metrics in Defense & Security, limiting cross-sectional validation, and reliance on capital-raise proxy methodology rather than market transaction data. Additional market comparables or recent transaction precedents within the narrower defense tech vertical would materially strengthen conviction in this range.
